findings.headline: 2,893 次「我不知道」——它是開場白，不是句點
findings.why: 英語職場把「我知道」跟「我猜」當成兩種不同等級的資訊，而講話的人有義務自己標記在哪一級。I don't know 就是那個標記器：它一出現，後面接的東西就自動被降級成推測，聽的人知道哪句要查證、哪句可以直接拿去做決定。所以位子越高的人講得越多，因為他一天要下的判斷越多、被回頭追究的機率越高，先把不確定的那塊圈掉，剩下 95% 的話才拿得到全額信任。它同時也是控場動作：劃掉一個範圍之後，剩下的地盤就是你的，你可以名正言順地只回答你真的有把握的那塊，而不是被整題拖著走。311 集裡有 308 集出現、每集中位數 8 次，代表這不是某個人的口頭禪，而是這個語言社群的預設協定。
findings.taiwan: 台灣人在英文會議被問到沒把握的事，最常見的三種反應是：含糊帶過（Yeah, I think so、Should be fine）、先把話講滿事後再私下補救、或是沉默等別人接話。代價是對方分不出你哪一句是查過的、哪一句是猜的，於是整場發言一起被打折——連你真的做過功課的那部分也拿不到分。更貴的是第二次：等你猜的那句後來被推翻，對方學到的不是「這一題他不知道」，而是「他講的都要再查一次」，你就從此被排除在需要即時判斷的會議之外。中文會議還能靠語氣、關係、事後補件救回來；英文會議只認你當下有沒有先標。

types.share: 約兩成二（非口頭禪用法中的三成一，最大宗）
types.note: 先用一句話把不知道的部分圈起來，同一口氣立刻交出你知道的那塊，句型固定是「I don't know X, but I can tell you / what I do know is / here's what I'm thinking Y」。補的料可以是資訊，也可以是下一步動作（let me get back to you）。這一型的效果是把「他答不出來」變成「他很清楚邊界在哪」，適合被問到跨部門、跨時間、你只掌握一半的問題。

examples.quote: I don't know what's behind his response, but I can tell you what's true for me.
examples.episode: How have I been complicit in creating the conditions I say I don’t want? | Jerry Colonna (CEO of Reboot, executive coach, former VC)

examples.quote: I'm not sure that it matches exactly to functions, but I can tell you what we're seeing more of, we need more of. We need more systems thinkers in a world with AI.
examples.episode: Netflix CPTO on AI and the future of product and tech roles | Elizabeth Stone

examples.quote: If you ask me a question, sometimes I don't know and I'll say, "Hey, let me get back to you." Sometimes I don't know and I'll say, "Hey, I don't know, but here's what I'm thinking."
examples.episode: Leveraging mentors to uplevel your career | Jules Walter (YouTube, Slack)

types.share: 約一成一（非口頭禪用法中的一成五）
types.note: 不是說「我不知道」，而是說「我不知道的是 why / what number / where it came from」，用 wh- 子句把缺口縮到一個具體的小問題。默認效果很強：你只圈掉那一塊，等於宣告其餘的你都掌握。常見的接法是下一句立刻講出你確實知道的相鄰事實，讓對方看見缺口的形狀而不是一片空白。

examples.quote: I don't know what that number is today. I know that it sort of went up and then down and then back up again.
examples.episode: Building better product roadmaps | Janna Bastow (Mind the Product, ProdPad)

examples.quote: If your name is Firefox, I have no idea what you did. You just took two words and put them together and made something up.
examples.episode: The art of building legendary brands | Arielle Jackson (Google, Square, Marketer in Residence at First Round Capital)

types.zh: 用「我不確定這樣對不對」提異議
types.share: 約一成（非口頭禪用法中的一成三）
types.note: 句型是 I don't know if / I'm not sure if 加一個完整主張，把「我反對」包裝成「我對這件事的把握不足」。攻擊的是命題不是人，對方可以順著補證據而不必先認錯，所以在會議上駁回一個提案時幾乎不會撕破臉。要注意它同時也把你的立場調弱了，用在你真的想擋下某件事時，後面必須立刻接一個具體的下一步。

examples.quote: I'm not sure if it's productive to continue to discussing right now. Let's talk about it again in a week.
examples.episode: Scripts for difficult conversations: Giving hard feedback, navigating defensiveness, the three questions you should end every meeting with, more | Alisa Cohn (executive coach)

examples.quote: I don't know if this is the right forum for explaining P values, because the definition of a P value is simple. What it hides is very complicated.
examples.episode: The ultimate guide to A/B testing | Ronny Kohavi (Airbnb, Microsoft, Amazon)

examples.quote: I don't know if it's the right way to describe it. I call it a kneeling where you have a thing, and it's not quite the right shape, and you put it out into the wild.
examples.episode: Linear’s secret to building beloved B2B products | Nan Yu (Head of Product)

types.share: 約 7%（非口頭禪用法中的一成）
types.note: 固定是 I don't know if you know / saw / remember X, but 加上你要講的東西。表面在講自己不知道，實際是在替對方留台階：萬一他早就知道，你沒有在說教；萬一他不知道，他也不必承認自己漏掉。這是把知識差距端上桌又不讓任何人丟臉的標準做法，在跨團隊同步、對外部客戶補背景時最好用。

examples.quote: I don't know if you saw this video, but basically John said that he was impressed, that he learns from Steve Jobs that there's a cabinet maker who finished the back of the cabinet, and how important that was.
examples.episode: Why we’re at the beginning of the AI hardware boom | Caitlin Kalinowski (ex–OpenAI, Meta, Apple)

examples.quote: Yeah, I mean, I don't know if you remember this, but there was this product called Our Stories, and essentially it was MyStory, but it was a public story.
examples.episode: How to win in the AI era: Ship a feature every week, embrace technical debt, ruthlessly cut scope, and create magic your competitors can't copy | Gaurav Misra (CEO and co-founder of Captions)

types.zh: 把未知升格成團隊的題目
types.note: 主詞從 I 換成 we：we don't know what's going on / we don't know if this will work。同一個未知從「我的能力缺口」變成「組織現在的資訊缺口」，接下來理所當然要配資源去補——語料裡這一型後面幾乎都直接接工作項目（做埋點、跑實驗、先承諾一段 discovery）。要做 roadmap、寫規格、跟老闆要人要時間時最該用這一型。

examples.quote: We don't know if we're going to actually end up going, and based on the results whether we're going to actually move forward with investing in that area, but that's a body of work we can commit to.
examples.episode: Behind the scenes of Calendly’s rapid growth | Annie Pearl (CPO)

examples.quote: We don't know. We can guess, but we don't really know where this is going to end up.
examples.episode: A rational conversation on where AI is actually going | Benedict Evans

types.note: I don't know how to do this，講的不是資訊缺口而是能力缺口，通常由職級最高的人講出來。語料裡它幾乎都緊接著求援或號召：找人、借腦、let's go figure it out。頻率最低但風險最高，適合用在你真的卡住、而拖下去的成本大於承認的成本時——重點是承認之後那半句一定要有動作。

examples.quote: At that point, I was an interim CMO at Nero and I'm like, "I don't know how to do this." And it actually earns you a lot more credit than you think.
examples.episode: Elena Verna on how B2B growth is changing, product-led growth, product-led sales, why you should go freemium not trial, what features to make free, and much more

examples.quote: There's a few other people where I'm like, I don't know how to solve this problem. Can I load this other person into my head and how would they approach it?
examples.episode: Making an impact through authenticity and curiosity | Ami Vora (CPO at Faire, ex-WhatsApp, FB, IG)

types.zh: 純口頭禪（沒有教學價值）
types.share: 約三成（最大單一用法，但不建議模仿）
types.note: 夾在句子中間、前後都是逗號的 I don't know，功能等同中文的「那個」「之類的」，用來拖一秒鐘找詞或標示後面的數字是隨口舉例（I don't know, 30 people、I don't know, let's say）。它跟認識論完全無關，也不會讓你聽起來比較謙虛。台灣人不必學這一型：母語者靠它爭取思考時間，非母語者用它只會讓句子更難懂，想拖時間用 Let me think for a second 更安全。

examples.quote: You're standing on top of the hill, you're looking down, you can see the, I don't know, rolling hills, the sheep, the grass, whatever.
examples.episode: Making an impact through authenticity and curiosity | Ami Vora (CPO at Faire, ex-WhatsApp, FB, IG)

examples.quote: So we interviewed Ben and it was a long day of interviews in a tiny glass conference room and Lyft was, I don't know, 30 people or something at the time.
examples.episode: How to build a high-performing growth team | Adam Fishman (Patreon, Lyft, Imperfect Foods)

examples.quote: In fact, actually, this is my email signature for, I don't know, for the last 20 years or so.
examples.episode: Microsoft CPO: If you aren’t prototyping with AI, you’re doing it wrong | Aparna Chennapragada

findings.en: Label it before you say it
findings.headline: 重話不是靠語氣軟化，是靠前面那個標籤買到的許可
findings.why: 英語會議裡的重話，殺傷力不在句子本身，而在對方怎麼解讀你的動機。一句沒有前綴的「That's not a strategy」，聽的人要自己去猜：你是在否定這份文件，還是在否定我這個人？猜錯的成本很高，所以他會先防禦。標籤句的作用就是把這個猜測環節收掉——它預先宣告了「這句話的射程有多遠」「哪些東西不在射程內」「我知道我接下來要說的不是共識」。範圍一旦被鎖死，對方就不需要用防禦來保護自己，重話才有地方落地。所以英語職場的火力上限不是由用詞決定的，是由你願不願意先花三秒鐘做這個宣告決定的。311 集裡有一半的集數出現這個動作，而且幾乎都出現在講者要下最硬的判斷之前。
findings.taiwan: 台灣人的直覺是把緩衝放在「後面」——先把重話丟出去，看對方臉色不對，再花五分鐘補「我不是那個意思」「我只是提出來討論」。但補在後面的緩衝救不了場：對方已經進入防禦，你後面講的每一句都被讀成退縮，於是重話也一起被收回，你等於什麼都沒說。另一種更常見的是連重話都不敢下，直接跳到「但是」，用一長串鋪陳把判斷藏在中間，主管聽完只記得你講了很多、沒記得你反對。代價是一樣的：你既沒有守住關係，也沒有把判斷送出去。

types.zh: 宣告立場強度：我知道這不是共識
types.note: 用 hot take、unpopular opinion、maybe this is a hot take 開頭，等於預先承認「這句話會有人不同意」。因為你自己先講了，對方就不必再花力氣提醒你，可以直接進入內容。這一型後面接的通常是對主流做法的整句否定——不是「這裡可以調整」，而是「這件事大部分人根本不需要」。

examples.quote: But my hot take is that for the vast majority of people, they probably do not need a coach.
examples.episode: How to make better decisions and build a joyful career | Ada Chen Rekhi (Notejoy, LinkedIn, SurveyMonkey)

examples.quote: I don't have Twitter, like hot take, I think Twitter ruins people's careers. I've already seen multiple careers ruined by Twitter.
examples.episode: The ultimate guide to Martech | Austin Hay (Reforge, Ramp, Runway)

examples.quote: This might be my hot take, but we do almost no estimating in order to hit deadlines. What we do is we ship as early as we can.
examples.episode: Linear’s secret to building beloved B2B products | Nan Yu (Head of Product)

types.zh: 先拆稻草人：我不是在說那個極端
types.note: 結構固定是「I'm not saying［最極端的解讀］, but［我真正的主張］」。先把對方最可能拿來反駁你的極端版本親手拆掉，剩下的火力就全打在真正的爭點上。93 次裡有 68 次後面直接接 but / however / what I'm saying is——這個標籤幾乎不會單獨出現，它存在的唯一目的就是替後面那句重話清出路。

examples.quote: I'm not saying we should go back to the early 90's, but I'm saying it wasn't always like this. The whole frontier of productivity at the time felt like it was just taking us in the wrong direction.
examples.episode: Behind the founder: Drew Houston (Dropbox)

types.zh: 先讓一步再翻盤：好，但那不是重點
types.note: 用 don't get me wrong 或 to be fair 先把對方的功勞、優點、合理之處認掉，證明你不是沒看見。認完之後那個 but 才有份量——因為你已經排除了「他只是沒搞懂」這個解釋。這一型後面接的常常是把整件事降級：不是說它不好，是說它不重要、不值得投資、不該用這個名字稱呼。

examples.quote: Now to be fair, Slack with their magic link, did a cool thing with the forgot password flow. That was a nice innovative thing that I think moved the industry forward. So if you want to do discovery on that, great, but you probably don't have to.
examples.episode: Teresa Torres on how to interview customers, automating continuous discovery, the opportunity solution tree framework, making the case for user research, common interviewing mistakes, and much more

examples.quote: And don't get me wrong, I think there's a lot of product folks out there who enjoy that modality of work, I'm not one of them.
examples.episode: Relentless curiosity, radical accountability, and HubSpot’s winning growth formula | Christopher Miller (VP of Product, Growth and AI)

types.zh: 限定射程：這句話只在這個範圍內成立
types.note: caveat 是唯一一個「先劃界線、界線內就講到底」的標籤。因為適用範圍被明確框住，框內的話反而可以講得斬釘截鐵——連「研究顯示這個做法沒有效」這種等級的斷言，都可以掛在一句 I would caveat 底下送出去。台灣人習慣用「可能」「某種程度上」把不確定性攤在整句話裡；英語職場是把不確定性集中扔進 caveat，讓主句保持乾淨。

examples.quote: I would caveat to say, interviews, actually we know, don't predict job performance. So, very little to no evidence would say interviews will predict how I perform on the job.
examples.episode: Using behavioral science to improve your product | Kristen Berman (Irrational Labs)

examples.quote: I do want to apply a pretty severe caveat here though, which is, a decision log is not a replacement for building products. It's a additional complimentary thing that you can be doing on your own.
examples.episode: Unorthodox PM wisdom: Automating user insights, unselling job candidates, logging every decision, more | Kevin Yien (Stripe, Square, Mutiny)

examples.quote: One thing to caveat is you do not get paid until you are approved by finance, and procurement has a signature on the contract. Meaning don't start any work.
examples.episode: "Sell the alpha, not the feature": The enterprise sales playbook for $1M to $10M ARR | Jen Abel

types.zh: 定調防誤讀：先把我沒有在主張的事切掉
types.note: 講者自己用 to be clear 把一個容易被誤植到自己頭上的立場切掉，通常出現在他正要講一句聽起來很極端、或很容易被斷章取義的話前後。功能不是澄清事實，是搶在對方腦補之前先定調——把話語權從「你會怎麼理解我」拿回到「我說了什麼」。這一型是唯一常見於連任何緩衝都不加的硬結論旁邊的標籤。

examples.quote: And to be clear, I don't think it's actually that dangerous right now.
examples.episode: Benjamin Mann

examples.quote: And to be clear, it's not easy to be a PM. It's not an entry level job.
examples.episode: Brandon Chu on building product at Shopify, how writing changed the trajectory of his career, the habits that make you a great PM, pros and cons of being a platform PM, how Shopify got through Covid

examples.quote: I do want to be clear, it's one leader and their team who are accountable and responsible.
examples.episode: Unpacking Amazon’s unique ways of working | Bill Carr (author of Working Backwards)

types.zh: 複述定錨：我先把你的話講一次，再處理它
types.share: 約 11%（32/299 次，30 集）——幾乎全是主持人使用
types.note: 「Just to be clear, you're saying ⋯⋯?」是先把對方的主張用自己的話壓成一句可攻擊的形狀，等對方點頭之後才動手。這一步做完，後面的反駁就不會被賴成「你誤會我的意思」——射程是他自己確認過的。台灣人開會時最常跳過的就是這一步，結果整場都在爭論彼此到底講了什麼。

examples.quote: And so just to be clear, you're saying 20 to 30% of people come back the next day?
examples.episode: How to find hidden growth opportunities in your product | Albert Cheng (Duolingo, Grammarly, Chess.com)

examples.quote: I guess just to be clear, are these the same thing in your mind with different words?
examples.episode: Business strategy with Hamilton Helmer (author of 7 Powers)
